mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the CPIAUCSL index above 210 signals rising inflation expectations, prompting market anticipation of higher interest rates and compressing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns do not turn negative when CPIAUCSL crosses above 210, or the t-test p-value exceeds 0.05 in such instances.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate and a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicate tightening monetary policy in a strengthening labor market, fostering growth expectations and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases and UNRATE decreases simultaneously
failure_condition: The interaction of FEDFUNDS and UNRATE movements does not correlate with positive returns, or the Rank IC exceeds 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A late-cycle expansion characterized by simultaneous high demand (GDPC1) and supply (INDPRO) growth signals overvaluation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain negative despite the late-cycle expansion regime, or the IC exceeds 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in UNRATE below 4.5% indicates a tightening labor market, boosting productivity and corporate profits, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns do not rise when UNRATE falls below 4.5%, or the IC remains above 0.03 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in HOUST below 1100 signals weakening demand for goods and services, leading to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns do not turn negative when HOUST crosses below 1100, or the IC exceeds 0.03 over any 3-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in INDPRO (supply) alongside a decline in FEDFUNDS (monetary easing) indicates expanding production capacity and lower borrowing costs, fostering growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases and FEDFUNDS decreases simultaneously
failure_condition: The combined effect of INDPRO and FEDFUNDS movements does not correlate with positive returns, or the IC exceeds 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in FEDFUNDS above 4.8% during a monetary tightening cycle signals stricter monetary policy, which may initially boost growth expectations but ultimately compresses equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns do not increase when FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.8%, or the IC remains below 0.03 over any 1-year rolling window.
